_comment: PINNED ceyx native-decoder release consumed by scripts/build_apps.py.
The tag fixes WHICH GitHub release the prebuilt libraries come from; the
sha256 values fix WHICH BYTES, because a tag can be moved and an asset
re-uploaded. build_apps.py downloads by tag URL (no GitHub API call, so
anonymous rate limits cannot fail a pinned build) and refuses to place a
library whose sha256 does not match.
Upstream publishes ONE .tar.gz per component/platform, so each entry pins:
archive + sha256    the release asset, gating the download;
libraries[]         member (path inside the tarball) -> artifact (on-disk
name) + the sha256 of that EXTRACTED file. Those are
re-checked after extraction and are read as data by
scripts/ci/assertions.py (H-DECODER-DEPS / -HASH), so
the packaged app is judged against this same file.
libraries[].uuid    OPTIONAL, Mach-O members only (macOS .dylib). The
LC_UUID build identifier, read via `dwarfdump --uuid`
by the same tool that writes sha256
(update_ceyx_pin_latest in build_apps.py). Exists
because Xcode's CocoaPods embed step re-signs
libheif.1.dylib and libde265.0.dylib after fetch,
changing their bytes (and hence sha256) without
changing their identifier. H-DECODER-HASH
(scripts/ci/assertions.py) uses this as a stage-3
fallback ONLY when stage 1 (sha256) mismatches and
stage 2 (`codesign --verify` on the shipped file)
passes: a UUID match then reports the library as
verified 'by build identity, re-signed by packaging'
rather than by digest. This proves internal
consistency (the file's own recorded content hashes
still match its bytes), NOT provenance (that these
are the bytes the release actually published) --
provenance stays gated entirely at the fetch
boundary, the sha256-against-lock cross-check above.
Absent for non-Mach-O members (Windows/Linux); a
missing/mismatched uuid on a Mach-O member whose
sha256 also mismatches is a hard FAIL, same as today.
All five macOS members carry a uuid (liblcms2.2.dylib
was removed at the v0.1.24 repin, 2026-09-13 -- see
below), not only the two that get re-signed -- but
stage 3 only ever runs for a library whose stage-1
digest mismatched. For the three whose sha256 still
matches (decoder, jpeg, omp), their uuid is UNEXERCISED DATA: nothing
currently checks it, so its mere presence must not
be read as evidence that it was verified. It is
recorded for completeness/future use only.
'lock' pins the release's own artifacts.lock. Every fetched archive must
appear in that lock AND its digest must equal the pin's; a release that was
re-published cannot pass by rewriting just one of the two records. The lock's
own digest is pinned so a substituted lock cannot satisfy the cross-check.
Windows is an ATOMIC GROUP of four DLLs shipped inside one archive: the
decoder plus heif.dll and libde265.dll, which it dynamically imports (LGPL-3
requires libheif/libde265 stay separate shared libraries -- see ceyx
native/third_party/heif-dist-windows/PROVENANCE.md), plus libomp140.x86_64.dll
(added 2026-09-13, v0.1.24 repin) for the same reason: the decoder DLL
imports it too, and this was a PRE-EXISTING latent gap -- v0.1.23's decoder
already imported it but the v0.1.23 archive did not carry it, so shipping
Windows builds relied on it being present from an MSVC/VC++ redistributable
on the target machine; v0.1.24 ships the DLL inside the archive for the
first time, closing that one gap -- but NOT making the placed set
self-contained: libomp140.x86_64.dll itself imports VCRUNTIME140.dll and
VCRUNTIME140_1.dll (verified via `objdump -p` against the published
asset), and NEITHER is in the archive or an OS default; both still
require a Visual C++ redistributable on the target machine. This is a
strict improvement (one of two missing runtime deps closed), not a
complete fix. A Windows install
missing any of these dependencies fails at DynamicLibrary.open with an error
naming only the decoder, so all four are extracted and verified together or
none is placed. Linux uses a one-element list so there is exactly one code
path.
Everything except 'linux', 'windows', 'macos-arm64' and 'macos-x86_64' is
VERIFIED BUT NOT PLACED. For 'android' the destination
(plugin/android/src/main/jniLibs) is a committed
upstream tree this script must not overwrite. The dist entries are consumed
by ceyx's OWN native build, not by a halcyon build: heif's runtime DLLs
already travel inside the windows decoder archive, and libwebp/libjxl are
STATIC-ONLY dists (.lib on Windows, .a on Linux) linked at ceyx build time,
so there is nothing for halcyon to place. Pinning them anyway keeps every
archive this project's platforms depend on inside the integrity +
provenance check.
Each asset entry carries 'placed' (bool) and, when false, a one-line
'not_placed_reason' -- these are written by update_ceyx_pin_latest FROM
CEYX_FETCH_SPECS[ft]['place'] / ['not_placed_reason'] (single writer, so
the pin and the code cannot disagree). See each entry's own
not_placed_reason for why it is verified but not placed.
This file is edited by hand OR, deliberately, by
`python3 scripts/build_apps.py --ceyx-release latest|<tag>`, which downloads
the release's assets, records their real digests here, and STOPS without
building. The maintainer then reviews this diff and commits it. An upstream
release therefore cannot alter Halcyon's decoder without a visible,
reviewable change to this file. Use an explicit tag when the GitHub API's
mutable 'latest' flag lags the release you mean to pin.
sha256 provenance: pin moved to v0.1.7 on 2026-08-31 via
`python3 scripts/build_apps.py --ceyx-release v0.1.7` (an explicit tag, not
'latest' -- the API's mutable 'latest' flag lagged by a whole release when
the v0.1.6 pin was cut), which downloaded each archive from
https://github.com/jhangyu/ceyx/releases/download/v0.1.7/<asset>, checked it
against that release's artifacts.lock, and recorded the digests below.
v0.1.7 is the first tar.gz-ONLY release: it publishes no raw .so/.dll/.dylib
assets, and it adds libjxl dists for Linux and Windows. Every archive digest
below changed from v0.1.6 -- including heif.dll and libde265.dll, which were
rebuilt -- so this is a genuine re-derivation, not a tag relabel.
Evidence: tmp/verify/r7-fetch.txt (fetch+extract+verify, RC=0) and
tmp/verify/r7-redstate.txt (each gate proven to fail when tampered with).
Trust-on-first-use (same authority that serves the bytes): catches any
FUTURE substitution, not one predating this date.
macOS is now PINNED (HALCYON-MIGRATION campaign, 2026-09, tag v0.1.8): the
release asset itself carries five interdependent dylibs (decoder + jpeg +
heif + de265 + omp; liblcms2.2.dylib was REMOVED at the v0.1.24 repin,
2026-09-13, following upstream's announced lcms2 removal -- the archive
originally carried six, decoder + lcms2 + jpeg + heif + de265 + omp),
already @rpath-wired to each other,
so the release asset is self-contained in the same way the Linux/Windows
assets already are. Two entries, macos-arm64 and macos-x86_64, cover the
two architectures the release publishes separately (there is no
universal/fat archive; only macos-arm64 is exercised by CI today, since
the macOS CI leg runs on a single Apple-silicon runner -- macos-x86_64 is
unverified by any CI run and could be wrong without a build ever failing).
Codesigning the release asset is a SEPARATE, DEFERRED concern
(parking-lot, user-ruled): this project does not codesign anything it
fetches for any platform today, so an unsigned-but-hash-verified macOS
fetch is consistent with, not a regression from, how Linux/Windows
already work.
MINIMUM-OS REQUIREMENT of the bundled native stack (measured from the
actual LC_VERSION_MIN/LC_BUILD_VERSION load commands, not inferred from a
linker warning; figures below are as measured at the original six-dylib
set -- liblcms2.2.dylib was later REMOVED at the v0.1.24 repin, 2026-09-13,
so its own figure is no longer part of the shipped set, but the
requirement it did not drive is unaffected): the six-dylib set required
macOS 15 on Apple silicon and macOS 14 on Intel at runtime. This was NOT a
regression introduced by that migration -- the bundled OpenMP runtime
already required macOS 15 (both architectures) in the previously-committed
set, so the real floor was never actually 11; the decoder itself moves from
11 to 14 (Apple silicon)/14 (Intel), which is the only file whose own
minimum changes, while jpeg IMPROVES (15->14) and heif/de265 are unchanged
(11) -- lcms2 also improved (15->14) before its removal, but that fact no
longer describes the shipped set. Halcyon's own declared application-level
minimum (macOS 11,
macos/Runner/Configs/AppInfo.xcconfig / Info.plist LSMinimumSystemVersion)
is a SEPARATE, application-layer concern this migration does not alter
and is not corrected by anything in this file -- by user ruling, native
stack requirements and the application's declared minimum are not to be
conflated.

android.not_placed_reason: destination plugin/android/src/main/jniLibs is a committed upstream tree build_apps.py must not overwrite

heif-dist-windows.not_placed_reason: consumed by ceyx's own native build, not a halcyon build; heif's runtime DLLs already travel inside the windows decoder archive above

libjxl-dist-linux.not_placed_reason: consumed by ceyx's own native build; libjxl is a STATIC-ONLY dist (.a) linked at ceyx build time, nothing for halcyon to place

libjxl-dist-windows.not_placed_reason: consumed by ceyx's own native build; libjxl is a STATIC-ONLY dist (.lib) linked at ceyx build time, nothing for halcyon to place
